section.title: The ooSQLResult Class
section.para: The ooSQLResult class sets the result of the user defined SQL functions and aggregates written in Rexx, which are registered with the createFunction method of the ooSQLiteConnection class. Its methods are class methods: there are no ooSQLResult objects. Each method takes the SQLite context that the callback method receives as its second argument, and sets the result to a value of one type, or to an error.
The ooSQLValue class reads the arguments of those functions. The oosqlResult routines, such as oosqlResultInt, do the same as the methods of this class in the classic interface.

section.title: Method Table
section.para: The following table provides links to the documentation of the methods used in setting the result of a user defined SQL function with the ooSQLResult class.

row.entry: &changed11;Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a blob.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a floating point number.
Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail with an error message.
Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail with an error code.
Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail because it ran out of memory.
Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail because a string or a blob is too big.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a 32-bit integer.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a 64-bit integer.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to NULL.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a text.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a copy of one of the values passed to the function. The result keeps the datatype of the value.
Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a blob filled with zeros.

section.title: &changed11;blob (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a blob.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
&changed11;blob [required]
The data of the blob: a String, a Buffer, or a MutableBuffer object, as for the bindBlob method of the ooSQLiteStmt class, such as the String that blob returns, or a Pointer object to the data. Before ooSQLite 1.1 only a Pointer was accepted, so Rexx code could not return a blob made from its own data.
&changed11;size [optional with a String, Buffer, or MutableBuffer, required with a Pointer]
The number of bytes of the blob. With a String, a Buffer, or a MutableBuffer, the blob is made of the first size bytes of the data, which must be from 0 to the length of the data; if it is omitted, all the data is used. With a Pointer it is the number of bytes to copy from that address.
Returns 0. SQLite copies the data, so it can be discarded after the call.

What is said here applies to all the methods of the ooSQLResult class. They set the value that a user defined SQL function returns to the statement that invoked it, and they are used inside the callback methods registered with createFunction: the method of a function, and the final method of an aggregate. They are class methods: they are sent to the class, as in .ooSQLResult~int(context, 7). The sqlCntxt is the second argument of the callback method, a Pointer object that is only valid during that invocation of the method.
The functionality of the blob method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_blob API.
The oosqlResultBlob routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a SQL function, fromHex, that turns a hexadecimal string into a blob:
rc = db~createFunction("fromHex", .HexFunctions~new, 1, "fromHex") rows = db~exec("SELECT typeof(fromHex('CAFE')) AS t, hex(fromHex('CAFE')) AS h;", .true) say rows[1]['T'] rows[1]['H'] /* Output: blob CAFE */
::class HexFunctions ::method fromHex use arg db, context, userData, value .ooSQLResult~blob(context, .ooSQLValue~text(value)~x2c) return 0

section.title: double (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a floating point number.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
value [required]
The number. It is converted to a double precision floating point number.
Returns 0.
See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
Raises a syntax error if value is not a number.
The functionality of the double method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_double API.
The oosqlResultDouble routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a withTax function that adds a 21 percent tax to a price. A NULL price gives a NULL result:
rc = db~createFunction("withTax", .Prices~new, 1, "withTax") rows = db~exec("SELECT name, quote(withTax(price)) AS p FROM foods;", .true) do row over rows say row['NAME']':' row['P'] end /* Output: Bagels: 1.5125 Bagels, raisin: 1.815 Bacon: 4.5375 Cheese: NULL */
::class Prices ::method withTax use arg db, context, userData, price if .ooSQLValue~type(price) == .ooSQLite~SQLNULL then .ooSQLResult~null(context) else .ooSQLResult~double(context, .ooSQLValue~double(price) * 1.21) return 0

section.title: error (Class method)
section.para: Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail with an error message.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
errMsg [required]
The text of the error message.
Returns 0.

The statement that invoked the function fails with the code ERROR, and errMsg is its error message. errorCode sets another error code; when it is invoked after error, the message is kept. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the error method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_error API.
The oosqlResultError routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a checkPrice function that fails when a food has no price:
rc = db~createFunction("checkPrice", .Prices~new, 2, "checkPrice") say db~exec("SELECT checkPrice(name, price) FROM foods;") say db~lastErrCode db~lastErrMsg /* Output: 1 1 SQLite Error: rc = 1, Cheese has no price */
::class Prices ::method checkPrice use arg db, context, userData, name, price if .ooSQLValue~type(price) == .ooSQLite~SQLNULL then .ooSQLResult~error(context, .ooSQLValue~text(name) 'has no price') else .ooSQLResult~value(context, price) return 0

section.title: errorCode (Class method)
section.para: Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail with an error code.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
errCode [required]
The error code, one of the Result Code constants, such as CONSTRAINT.
Returns 0.

The statement that invoked the function fails with errCode. The error message is the one set by error, if it was invoked before; otherwise, it is the standard message for the code. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the errorCode method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_error_code API.
The oosqlResultErrorCode routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example makes a function fail with the code CONSTRAINT and its own message:
rc = db~createFunction("costly", .Prices~new, 1, "costly") say db~exec("SELECT costly(price) FROM foods;") say db~lastErrCode db~lastErrMsg /* Output: 19 19 SQLite Error: rc = 19, Bacon is too expensive */
::class Prices ::method costly use arg db, context, userData, price if .ooSQLValue~double(price) > 3 then do .ooSQLResult~error(context, 'Bacon is too expensive') .ooSQLResult~errorCode(context, .ooSQLite~CONSTRAINT) end else .ooSQLResult~value(context, price) return 0

section.title: errorNoMem (Class method)
section.para: Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail because it ran out of memory.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
Returns 0.
The statement that invoked the function fails with the code NOMEM and the message out of memory. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the errorNoMem method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_error_nomem API.
The oosqlResultErrorNoMem routine does the same in the classic interface.
See the example of errorTooBig, which works in the same way.

section.title: errorTooBig (Class method)
section.para: Makes a user defined SQL function, or the final step of an aggregate, fail because a string or a blob is too big.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
Returns 0.
The statement that invoked the function fails with the code TOOBIG and the message string or blob too big. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the errorTooBig method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_error_toobig API.
The oosqlResultErrorTooBig routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a shortName function that does not accept names longer than 10 characters:
rc = db~createFunction("shortName", .Texts~new, 1, "shortName") say db~exec("SELECT shortName(name) FROM foods;") say db~lastErrMsg /* Output: 18 SQLite Error: rc = 18, string or blob too big */
::class Texts ::method shortName use arg db, context, userData, name text = .ooSQLValue~text(name) if length(text) > 10 then .ooSQLResult~errorTooBig(context) else .ooSQLResult~text(context, text) return 0

section.title: int (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a 32-bit integer.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
value [required]
The whole number, which must fit in 32 bits: from -2147483648 to 2147483647. Use int64 for larger numbers.
Returns 0.
See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
Raises a syntax error if value is not a whole number that fits in 32 bits.
The functionality of the int method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_int API.
The oosqlResultInt routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a words function that counts the words of a text, and uses it in a WHERE clause:
rc = db~createFunction("words", .Texts~new, 1, "words") rows = db~exec("SELECT name, words(name) AS w FROM foods WHERE words(name) > 1;", .true) say rows[1]['NAME']':' rows[1]['W'] 'words' /* Output: Bagels, raisin: 2 words */
::class Texts ::method words use arg db, context, userData, text .ooSQLResult~int(context, words(.ooSQLValue~text(text))) return 0

section.title: int64 (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a 64-bit integer.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
value [required]
The whole number, which must fit in 64 bits: from -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807.
Returns 0.
The method that computes the value may need a higher NUMERIC DIGITS setting than the default of 9, as the example does. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
Raises a syntax error if value is not a whole number that fits in 64 bits.
The functionality of the int64 method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_int64 API.
The oosqlResultInt64 routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a factorial function. The factorial of 20 does not fit in 32 bits:
rc = db~createFunction("factorial", .Numbers~new, 1, "factorial") rows = db~exec("SELECT factorial(20) AS f, typeof(factorial(20)) AS t;", .true) say rows[1]['F'] rows[1]['T'] /* Output: 2432902008176640000 integer */
::class Numbers ::method factorial use arg db, context, userData, n numeric digits 20 f = 1 do i = 2 to .ooSQLValue~int(n) f = f * i end .ooSQLResult~int64(context, f) return 0

section.title: null (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to NULL.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
Returns 0.
A function whose method sets no result also returns NULL, but setting it explicitly makes the intent clear. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the null method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_null API.
The oosqlResultNull routine does the same in the classic interface.
See the examples of double and value.

section.title: text (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a text.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
txt [required]
The string. SQLite expects the text to be UTF-8. The text ends at its first NUL character, if it has one: use blob for data that can contain NUL characters.
Returns 0.
SQLite copies the text. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the text method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_text API.
The oosqlResultText routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines an initials function that returns the first letter of each word of a name:
rc = db~createFunction("initials", .Texts~new, 1, "initials") rows = db~exec("SELECT name, initials(name) AS i FROM foods;", .true) do row over rows say row['NAME']':' row['I'] end /* Output: Bagels: B Bagels, raisin: BR Bacon: B Cheese: C */
::class Texts ::method initials use arg db, context, userData, name text = .ooSQLValue~text(name) initials = '' do i = 1 to words(text) initials ||= left(word(text, i), 1)~upper end .ooSQLResult~text(context, initials) return 0

section.title: &changed11;value (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a copy of one of the values passed to the function. The result keeps the datatype of the value.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
value [required]
One of the values that SQLite passes to the callback method: the fourth and following arguments of the method of a function, or the fifth and following arguments of the step method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
Returns 0.

The value must be one of the values passed to the current invocation of the method, or a value returned by columnValue while its statement stays on the same result row. &changed11;Any other Pointer raises a syntax error, 88.900, and so does a value passed to an invocation that has ended, or a value whose statement has been finalized (see Handles). Before ooSQLite 1.1 they could crash the interpreter. See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
Raises a syntax error if value is not a Pointer object.
The functionality of the value method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_value API.
The oosqlResultValue routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a firstOf function, with any number of arguments, that returns the first one that is not NULL. The result keeps its type:
rc = db~createFunction("firstOf", .Values~new, -1, "firstOf") sql = "SELECT name, firstOf(price, type_id, 'none') AS v," - "typeof(firstOf(price, type_id, 'none')) AS t FROM foods WHERE id > 2;" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['NAME']':' row['V'] '('row['T']')' end /* Output: Bacon: 3.75 (real) Cheese: 3 (integer) */
::class Values ::method firstOf use arg db, context, userData, ... do i = 4 to arg() if .ooSQLValue~type(arg(i)) \== .ooSQLite~SQLNULL then do .ooSQLResult~value(context, arg(i)) return 0 end end .ooSQLResult~null(context) return 0

section.title: zeroBlob (Class method)
section.para: Sets the result of a user defined SQL function, or of the final step of an aggregate, to a blob filled with zeros.

listitem.para:
The arguments are:
sqlCntxt [required]
The SQLite context, the second argument of the callback method of a function, or of the final method of an aggregate. See the remarks of blob.
size [required]
The size of the blob, in bytes. A negative size is the same as 0.
Returns 0.
See the remarks of blob for when and how the result is set.
The functionality of the zeroBlob method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_result_zeroblob API.
The oosqlResultZeroBlob routine does the same in the classic interface.

This example defines a blank function, and uses it to set the picture of a food to 8 zero bytes:
rc = db~createFunction("blank", .Values~new, 1, "blank") rc = db~exec("UPDATE foods SET picture = blank(8) WHERE id = 1;") sql = "SELECT length(picture) AS l, hex(picture) AS h FROM foods WHERE id =" - "1;" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) say rows[1]['L'] rows[1]['H'] /* Output: 8 0000000000000000 */
::class Values ::method blank use arg db, context, userData, size .ooSQLResult~zeroBlob(context, .ooSQLValue~int(size)) return 0
